Ph.D. Program in Applied Mathematics
Ph.D. Program in Applied Mathematics
At Georgetown University, our Ph.D. in Applied Mathematics is more than a program; it’s a launchpad for discovery, innovation, and impact. Our program is designed to prepare you for diverse career paths, whether in academia, industry, or government, while offering a supportive environment where mentorship, creativity, and intellectual curiosity thrive. Join us to transform your passion for applied mathematics into solutions that make a difference.
Quick Links
Request Information
How to Apply
Apply Now
Institutional FundingAll admitted students will be offered a Ph.D. Assistantship, which covers full tuition, health insurance, and a stipend. This support allows you to focus on your studies and research, moving confidently through each stage of the Ph.D.
Campus and BeyondYou will engage in cutting-edge research with faculty. Beyond the classroom, you’ll collaborate with peers, present at conferences, and contribute to projects that reach from the Hilltop campus to the wider world.
When to Apply
Applications for Fall 2027 admission are now open, with a deadline of January 15, 2027. Our Ph.D. program welcomes motivated scholars ready to push the boundaries of mathematics. Whether you’re finishing your bachelor’s in the mathematical sciences or building on research experience, you’ll find a community ready to challenge, inspire, and support you. No master’s degree required.
Discover More About the Process
Ph.D. Requirements
The program begins with nine courses (27 credits)—a rigorous foundation completed in the first two years, including four core courses in year one. After passing comprehensive exams, students transition from coursework to original research, forming dissertation committees and advancing toward their dissertations.
Learn More About the Requirements
Explore the Coursework
Your Student Experience
The Ph.D. journey at Georgetown is rigorous but also rich with support, connection, and discovery. Students benefit from:
— Collaborative environment encouraging peer learning
— Workshops, seminars, and colloquia featuring guest speakers from academia and industry
— Teach and mentor undergraduates, building both skill and confidence
— Social and professional networks beyond the Hilltop
